counteract

/kown-ter-AKT/ - the stress falls on AKT · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Counteract means to act against something and cancel out its effect.

A spoonful of honey counteracts the bitterness of the tea without hiding its flavor.

Worked Example

To counteract the glare that washed out the morning exhibits, the curator hung amber film over the skylights — the sun kept shining, but its effect on the paintings was cancelled.

Counteract is different from 'prevent' or 'undo': it doesn't stop a force from existing or reverse it afterward. It works against the force in real time, pushing back so the net effect comes out to nothing.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

counterbalance: To counterbalance is to set an equal weight or force against something — static and mechanical, like the counterweight in a crane. To counteract is active and ongoing: you push against a force while it operates, so its effect cancels in real time.

offset: To offset is to balance one thing against another so the totals come out even — an accounting word for gains covering losses. To counteract is more physical and immediate: an opposing action fights a live force directly, cancelling its effect as it happens.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

reinforce: to make an effect stronger instead of pushing against it

worsen: to deepen the very effect you could have opposed

Where it sits · how fully the effect is undone — dampen → counteract → negate

dampen vs. counteract: Dampening an effect is milder than counteracting it — the force is softened a little, but most of it still gets through.

negate vs. counteract: Negating an effect goes even further than counteracting it — nothing is left at all, as if the force had never acted.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — counter-

Prefix — counter-: against, in opposition

Root — act

Root — act: to do, to drive (Latin agere, actus)

Put it together

Put it together: Counter- (against) + act (to do, drive) = to act against. The word is its own diagram: something is acting on the world, and you act back in the opposite direction until the two cancel out.

Use the root in a new word: react

Use the root in a new word: react: Vinegar and baking soda react instantly, each acting back on the other in a hiss of foam.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / technical

Counteract is the working word of chemists, doctors, and engineers — one force deployed against another so the effect cancels. Use 'offset' for accounting-flavored balance and 'undo' for repair after the fact. Its unit-mate neutralize goes to the source and leaves it harmless; counteract leaves the source running and fights its effect to a draw.
